Al-Walibi narrated from him: It is an oath which God swore by, and it is one of the names of God, the Exalted.

Qatada said: Ha Mim is one of the names of the Qur'an.

Mujahid said: It is the openings of the surahs.

Al-Qurazi said: God swore by His forbearance and His dominion that He would not punish anyone who returns to Him saying, "There is no god but God," sincerely from his heart.

Al-Sha'bi said: It is the emblem (sha'ar) of the surah.

Ata' ibn Abi Muslim al-Khurasani said: The Ha is the opening of the names of God: Halim, Hamid, Hayy, Hannan, and Hakim; and the Mim is the opening of His names: Malik, Majid, and Mannan. What supports this is what was narrated from Anas ibn Malik, who said: A Bedouin asked the Messenger of God (ﷺ) what Ha Mim is, "for we do not know it in our language?" He said: "The beginning of the names and the openings of the surahs."

Al-Dahhak and al-Kisa'i said: Its meaning is "decreed what is to be," as if they intended to indicate that it is read ḥumma with a damma on the ha and a shadda on the mim.

﴿The revelation of the Book is from God, the Almighty, the All-Knowing.﴾ The readers differed regarding His saying "Ha Mim." Ii (ʿIsa), Hamza, al-Kisa'i, and Khalaf read it with a kasra on the ha wherever it occurs, and Yahya and Hammad narrated similarly from Abu Bakr, from Asim. Abu Ja'far, Abu Ubayd, Abu Hatim, and Ibn Dhakwan read it between fatha and kasra. Bakr ibn Sahl al-Dimyati and Isma'il al-Nakhkhas narrated similarly from Warsh, from Nafi'. The rest read it with a fatha.

﴿Forgiver of sin﴾: Ibn Abbas said: to the one who says, "There is no god but God."

﴿And Acceptor of repentance﴾: from those who say, "There is no god but God."

﴿Severe in punishment﴾: for the one who does not say, "There is no god but God."

﴿Owner of bounty﴾: the possessor of wealth, toward the one who does not say, "There is no god but God."

Al-Dahhak said: "Owner of favors (dhi al-manan)."
Qatada said: "Owner of blessings (dhi al-ni'am)."
Al-Suddi said: "Owner of abundance (dhi al-sa'a)."
Al-Hasan said: "Owner of grace (dhi al-fadl)."
Ibn Zayd said: "Owner of power (dhi al-qudra)."

The root of ṭawl is a bounty whose duration extends over its recipient. It is said: "O God, extend (ṭall) over us," meaning, "Bestow upon us and show grace." From it comes the word for benefit: ṭa'il. It is said in speech: "I gained nothing (ma khaliyat min fulan bi-ṭa'il) from so-and-so, and I obtained nothing (ma ḥaẓiyat minhu bi-na'il) from him," meaning, "I found no benefit from him."

We were informed by al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Fanjawayh: Ahmad ibn Ja'far ibn Hamdan narrated to us: Yusuf ibn Abd Allah ibn Mahan narrated to us: Musa ibn Isma'il narrated to us: Hammad narrated to us, from Thabit, who said: "I was beside the pavilion of Mus'ab ibn al-Zubayr in a place where animals did not pass. I had begun reciting ﴿Ha Mim. The revelation of the Book is from God, the Almighty, the All-Knowing﴾ when a man passed by on a riding animal. When I recited ﴿Forgiver of sin﴾, he said: 'Say: O Forgiver of sin, forgive my sin.'" I recited ﴿And Acceptor of repentance﴾. He said: "Say: O Acceptor of repentance, accept my repentance." I recited ﴿Severe in punishment﴾. He said: "Say: O Severe in punishment, pardon me from my punishment." I recited ﴿Owner of bounty﴾. He said: "Say: O Owner of bounty, shower upon me something good." Then he turned right and left, and I saw nothing.

The people of allusion (ahl al-isharah) said: ﴿Forgiver of sin﴾ is grace, ﴿Acceptor of repentance﴾ is promise, and ﴿Severe in punishment﴾ is justice.

﴿There is no god but Him; to Him is the final return.﴾ Singular. The word al-tawb may be a verbal noun (masdar), and it is possible that it is the plural of tawba, like dawma and dawwam, and 'awma and 'awwam.

We were informed by Abd Allah ibn Hamid, who read it to him: Muhammad ibn Khalid ibn al-Hasan narrated to us: Dawud ibn Sulayman informed us: Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us: Kathir ibn Hisham narrated to us: Ja'far ibn Burqan informed us: Yazid ibn al-Asamm narrated to us:

That a man who was strong was being sent to Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, because of his strength. He was from the people of Syria. Umar missed him and asked about him, and it was said to him: "He keeps drinking this drink." So Umar called his scribe and said: "Write: From Umar ibn al-Khattab to so-and-so ibn so-and-so: Peace be upon you. I praise God to you, there is no god but He, ﴿In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. Ha Mim. The revelation of the Book is from God, the Almighty, the All-Knowing. Forgiver of sin, and Acceptor of repentance, Severe in punishment, Owner of bounty. There is no god but He; to Him is the final return.﴾" He sealed the letter and gave it to his messenger and said: "Do not give the letter to him until you find him sober." Then he commanded those around him to pray that God would turn toward him with His heart and accept his repentance. When the letter reached the man, he began to read it and say: "God has promised me forgiveness and warned me of His punishment." He kept repeating it to himself until he wept, then he stopped drinking, and his repentance and condition became good. When Umar learned of his situation, he said: "Thus do, when you see your brother slip into an error: set him right, help him to succeed, and pray to God to accept his repentance. Do not be helpers of Satan against him."

﴿None dispute concerning the signs of God except those who disbelieve.﴾ That is, they argue against them, contend with them, and persist in denying them.

We were informed by Abd Allah ibn Hamid: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub informed us: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us: Khalid ibn al-Walid narrated to us: Abu Ja'far al-Razi narrated to us, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-Aliyah, who said: "Two verses are among the most severe against those who dispute about the Qur'an: ﴿None dispute concerning the signs of God except those who disbelieve﴾ and ﴿Indeed, those who differ about the Book are in extreme schism﴾."

We were informed by Abd Allah ibn Hamid: Muhammad ibn Khalid narrated to us: Dawud ibn Sulayman informed us: Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us: al-Husayn ibn Ali al-Ju'fi narrated to us, from Za'ida, from Layth, from Sa'd ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Salama, from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Indeed, disputing about the Qur'an is disbelief."

﴿So let not their movement throughout the land deceive you.﴾ That is, their going about in the land for trade and their remaining there despite their disbelief. God gives them respite but does not neglect them. A parallel is ﴿Let not the movement of those who disbelieve through the land deceive you; it is a little enjoyment﴾. Then He said: ﴿The people of Noah denied before them, and the factions after them.﴾ That is, after the people of Noah. ﴿And every nation plotted against its messenger to seize him﴾, that is, to kill him.

Al-Farra' said: "It should have said 'against its messenger' (bi-rasuliha), and so it is in the reading of Abd Allah, but He meant by 'nation' the men, so He said 'against their messenger' (bi-rasulihim)."

﴿And they argued with falsehood to refute thereby the truth﴾, that is, to invalidate and remove the truth by it. ﴿So I seized them; then how was My punishment?﴾ ﴿And thus the word of your Lord has come true against those who disbelieved: that they are companions of the Fire.﴾ Those who bear the Throne and those around it are the angels.

Ibn Abbas said: The bearers of the Throne, from the ankle of one of them to the base of his feet, is a journey of five hundred years. He said: The distance between their feet in the lowest earth and their heads has pierced the Throne; they are in humility, not raising their gaze. They are more fearful than the people of the seventh heaven, and the people of the seventh heaven are more fearful than the people of the heaven next to them, and that next is more fearful than the one after it.

Mujahid said: Between the angels and the Throne there are seventy veils of light.

We were informed by Ibn Fanjawayh al-Dinawari: Makhlad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: al-Hasan ibn Alawiyya narrated to us: Isma'il ibn Isa narrated to us: Ishaq informed me, from Muqatil, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn Abbas, who said: When God created the bearers of the Throne, He said to them: "Bear My Throne." They were unable, so He created with each angel of them helpers like the hosts of the angels in the heavens and the creatures on the earth, and He said: "Bear My Throne." They were unable. So He created with each one of them the hosts of the seven heavens and seven earths and what is in the earth, as many as the pebbles and the dust, and said: "Bear My Throne." They were unable, and He said: "Say: There is no power and no might except by God."

They said: "There is no power and no might except by God; we are able to lift the Throne of our Lord." He said: Their feet sank into the seventh earth upon the moisture of the dust and did not settle. So the name of one of His names was written upon the foot of each angel, and their feet became firm.

Shahr ibn Hawshab narrated from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Do not reflect on His greatness, but reflect on what God has created of the angels. Indeed, an angel called Israfil is a corner of the corners of the Throne, upon his shoulder, and his feet are in the lowest earth, and his head has passed through seven heavens, and he dwindles from the greatness of God, the Exalted, until he becomes like something lowly."

Musa ibn Uqba narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir ibn Abd Allah, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "I have been permitted to tell of an angel from the angels of God, one of the bearers of His Throne, the distance between the lobe of his ear and his shoulder being a journey of seven hundred years."

In a report: God commanded all the angels to go forth and return with greetings to the bearers of His Throne, as a preference for them over the rest of the angels. This is the description of the bearers of the Throne.

As for the description of the Throne:

Luqman ibn Amir narrated from his father, who said: God created the Throne from a green jewel. For the Throne there are a million thousand heads of ... and behind these are a hundred thousand rows of angels who have placed the right hand upon the left. None of them is without glorifying God with praise, not one glorifying what another glorifies. The distance between the wings of one of them is a journey of three hundred years, and the distance between the lobe of his ear and his shoulder is four hundred years. God veiled Himself between Himself and the angels who are around the Throne with seventy veils of fire, seventy veils of darkness, seventy veils of light, seventy veils of white pearl, seventy veils of red ruby, seventy veils of green emerald, seventy veils of ice, seventy veils of water, seventy veils of hail, and what none knows but God, the Exalted.

He said: Each of the bearers of the Throne and those around it has four faces: the face of an ox, the face of a lion, the face of an eagle, and the face of a human. Each one of them has four wings: two wings with which he covers his face lest he look at the Throne and be struck senseless, and two wings with which he flies and is strengthened. They have no speech except glorification, praise, magnification, and exaltation.

Yazid al-Raqqashi said: God has angels around the Throne called "the sincere" (al-mukhlisun). Their eyes flow like rivers until the Day of Resurrection. They sway as if shaken by the fear of God. The Lord, majestic in His majesty, says to them: "O My angels, is it a fear that frightens you?" They say: "O our Lord, if the people of the earth had looked upon what we have looked upon of Your might and Your greatness, they would not have tasted food or drink, nor stretched out on their beds, and they would have gone out to the deserts lowing like cattle."

﴿They glorify their Lord with His praise, and believe in Him, and seek forgiveness for those who believe.﴾ This is an explanation of His saying ﴿and seek forgiveness for those on the earth﴾. ... ﴿Our Lord, You have encompassed all things in mercy and knowledge; so forgive those who repent and follow Your way, and protect them from the punishment of Hellfire.﴾ That is, "and they say: Our Lord." ﴿Encompassed all things in mercy and knowledge﴾ is in the accusative as an explanation. It was also said it is in the accusative by transfer (al-naql), meaning: "Your mercy and Your knowledge have encompassed all things. So forgive those who repent and follow Your way," that is, Your religion, "and protect them from the punishment of Hellfire."

Al-A'mash narrated from Ibrahim, who said: The companions of Abd Allah used to say: "The angels are better than Ibn al-Kawwa'." ﴿They ask forgiveness for those on the earth﴾, while Ibn al-Kawwa' testifies against them with disbelief. Ibn al-Kawwa' was a man of the Khawarij. He said: They did not like seeking forgiveness for anyone of the people of this qibla.

He also said: "We have found the most sincere servants of God toward the servants of God to be the angels, and we have found the most deceitful servants of God toward the servants to be Satan."

I heard Abu al-Qasim ibn Habib say: I heard my father say: I heard Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Muhammad al-Warraq say: I heard Yahya ibn Mu'adh al-Razi say to his companions when he recited this verse: "Understand it, for in the world there is nothing more hopeful than this."

﴿Our Lord, and admit them to gardens of perpetual residence which You promised them, and whoever was righteous among their fathers, their spouses, and their descendants. Indeed, You are the Almighty, the All-Wise.﴾ "Whoever" (man) is in the accusative in a grammatical position of coordination with the pronoun of "them" (hum) and the "mim" (mim al-jama'a).

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: A man will enter Paradise and say, "Where is my father, where is my mother, where is my child, where is my wife?"
It will be said, "They did not do deeds like yours."
He will say, "I used to do deeds for myself and for them."
It will be said, "Admit them into Paradise."

﴿And protect them from evil deeds﴾: that is, the various kinds of punishment. ﴿And whoever You protect from evil deeds on that Day, You have indeed shown him mercy. That is the great triumph.﴾

﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve will be called out on the Day of Resurrection while they are in the Fire, and they will have loathed themselves when they witnessed the punishment. It will be said to them: "The loathing of Allah toward you in the worldly life, when you were called to faith and you disbelieved, was greater than your loathing of yourselves today"﴾, at the arrival of the punishment upon you. ﴿When you were called to faith and you disbelieved.﴾

﴿They will say: "Our Lord, You have made us die twice and You have given us life twice."﴾

Ibn 'Abbas, Qatadah and al-Dahhak said: They were dead in the loins of their fathers, then Allah gave them life in the world, then He caused them the death that is unavoidable, then He gave them life for the Resurrection on the Day of Judgment. So there are two lives and two deaths. This is like His statement: ﴿How can you disbelieve in Allah, when you were dead and He gave you life?﴾ [Al-Baqarah 2:28] and so on.

Al-Suddi said: They were made to die in the world, then were given life in their graves, then they were questioned, then they were made to die in their graves, then they were given life in the Hereafter.

﴿So we have acknowledged our sins. Is there any way out?﴾, so that we may correct our deeds. Its parallel is His statement: ﴿Is there any way of return?﴾ [al-Shura 42:44]. ﴿That is because when Allah alone was invoked, you disbelieved﴾. In the speech there is an omitted element, which is understood from the apparent sense, its implied meaning being: "So you are answered that there is no way to that, which is the punishment and eternal abiding in the Fire, because when Allah alone was invoked in the world, you disbelieved in Him and denied that divinity belongs to Him alone, and you said: ﴿Has he made the gods into one God? Indeed, this is a strange thing.﴾" ﴿And if partners were associated with Him, you believed﴾: that is, you would believe in that polytheist and confirm him. I heard some scholars say: "And if partners were associated with Him after being returned to the world, you would believe in the polytheist," mentioning it in the interrogative form. Its parallel is His statement: ﴿And if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden﴾ [al-An'am 6:28].

﴿So the judgment belongs to Allah, the Most High, the Great.﴾

He is the One who shows you His signs and sends down for you provision from the sky, by the pouring down of rain; yet none remembers except one who turns back (in repentance). So call upon Allah, sincerely devoting to Him the religion (al-din): worship and obedience, even though the disbelievers dislike it. Rafi' al-Darajat (Exalted in Degrees): He is exalted in degrees, meaning He raises the levels of reward for the prophets and believers in Paradise.

Ibn 'Abbas said: "Rafi' al-samawat (the One who raises the heavens), and He is above everything, and nothing is above Him."

Dhu al-'Arsh (Lord of the Throne): its Creator and its Owner. Yulqi al-ruh (He casts down the Spirit): He sends down the revelation, and He called it "spirit" because by it hearts are given life, just as bodies are given life by spirits. Min amrihi (by His command): from His command, and it was said: by His order. 'Ala man yasha'u min 'ibadihi (upon whomever He wills of His servants), liyundhira yawm al-talaq (that he may warn of the Day of Meeting).

The reading of the common people (al-'amma) is with the yā' (ya), meaning that Allah, the Exalted, warns.

Al-Hasan read it with the tā' (ta), meaning: "that you (tundhir), O Muhammad, may warn of the Day of Meeting."

Abu al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl al-Faqih informed us: Abu al-'Abbas al-Asamm narrated to us: Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd Allah narrated to us: Abu Usama narrated to us: al-Mubarak ibn Fudala narrated to us, from 'Ali ibn Zayd, from Yusuf ibn Mihran, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying, the Exalted: liyundhira yawm al-talaq. He said: "It is the day when the people of the heavens and the people of the earth meet."

Qatada and Muqatil said: "The creation and the Creator meet on it."

Ibn Zayd: "The servants meet one another."

Maymun ibn Mihran: "The oppressor and the oppressed meet, and the disputants." It was also said: "The worshippers and those worshipped meet."

It was said: "A person meets his deeds on it."

Yawm hum barizun (the Day they will come forth): emerging from their graves, visible, with nothing concealing them. La yakhfa 'ala Allahi minhum (nothing about them is hidden from Allah) of their deeds and their states, shay' (anything). The place of "hum" is nominative as a subject (mubtada'), and "barizun" is its predicate. Limani al-mulk al-yawm (Whose is the dominion today?): this occurs at the annihilation of creation, and we have mentioned the reports concerning it.

Al-Hasan said: "He is the one who asks and the one who answers, for He says this when no one answers Him, so He answers Himself: Lillahi al-Wahid al-Qahhar (To Allah, the One, the Subduer), who subdued creation by death."

Shu'ayb informed us: Makki narrated to us: Abu al-Azhar narrated to us: Rawh narrated to us: Hammad narrated to us, from 'Asim ibn Bahdala, from Abu Wa'il, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: "Allah will gather the creation on the Day of Resurrection in one plain, a white land like a silver ingot, in which He has never been disobeyed. The first thing He will say is that a caller will call out: Whose is the dominion today? To Allah, the One, the Subduer."

Al-yawm tujza kullu nafsin bima kasabat, la zulma al-yawm, inna Allaha sari'u al-hisab (Today every soul will be recompensed for what it earned; there is no injustice today; indeed Allah is swift in reckoning). The first thing they will be disputing about is blood.

Wa-andhirhum yawm al-azifa (And warn them of the Day of the Approaching): meaning the Day of Resurrection. It was so named because it is near, since everything that is to come is near.

al-Nabigha said:

"The departure drew near, yet our riding-camels have not yet moved from our saddles, and it is as if..."

That is, it drew near. A similar verse is His saying: Azifat al-azifa (The Approaching Hour has drawn near), meaning the Resurrection has drawn near.

Idh al-qulubu ladaa al-hanajir (When the hearts reach the throats): from fear, the hearts have been dislodged and have risen from their chests, becoming lodged in their throats; so they neither return to their places nor leave their mouths to die, and they are not at ease. Its parallel is His saying: wa-af'idatuhum hawa' (and their hearts are a void). Kazimin (choking, suppressed): distressed, filled with fear and grief. Al-kazim is one who holds back something as it is within it, and from it comes kazama qirbatahu, when he tied its mouth. They have clamped their mouths shut over what is in their hearts of intense fear. Al-kazm is the churning of rage, fear, and grief within the heart when it becomes constricted by them.

The Arabs say of a narrow well and of a full water-vessel: "ma'un kazama and kazima." And from the hadith: "How will you be when Mecca is opened and its ... are filled?"

The poet said:

"They come forth from a narrow well... they carry 'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib."

Kazimin is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (hal) and as a qat' (a separated description).

Ma li al-zalimina min hamimin (The wrongdoers will have no intimate friend), qarib wa-sadiq (close relative and friend), and from it the relatives and close intimates are called hamma. Wa-la shafi'in yuta' (nor any intercessor who is obeyed), so that he may intercede for them.

Ya'lamu khA'inata al-a'yun (He knows the treachery of the eyes).

The author (al-Mu'arrikh) said: "There is inversion (taqdim and ta'khir) in it, meaning al-a'yun al-khA'inah (the treacherous eyes)." Ibn 'Abbas said: "It is the man who sits with a people, and a woman passes by, and he steals a glance at her."

Mujahid said: "It is the eyes' looking at what Allah has forbidden."

Qatada said: "It is the blinking of the eye and its closing regarding what Allah does not love or approve."

Wa-ma tukhfi al-sudur (and what the breasts conceal). Wallahu yaqdi bil-haqq (And Allah judges with truth), wa-alladhina yad'una min dunihi (and those they call upon besides Him), meaning the idols, la yaqdina bi-shay' (they judge nothing), because they know nothing and have no power over anything.

The people of Medina and Ayyub read "tad'una" with the tā' (you), and similarly Hisham narrated from the people of Syria; the rest read it with the yā' (they).

Inna Allaha huwa al-sami' al-basir (Indeed, Allah is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing).

Awa lam yasiru fi al-ardi fa-yanzuru kayfa kana 'aqibatu al-ladhina kanu min qablihim, kanu hum ashadda minhum quwwatan (Have they not traveled through the earth and seen how was the end of those before them, who were greater than them in strength).

The common readers read it with the hā' (hum).

Ibn 'Amir read "minkum" with the kāf (you), and likewise it is in their codices (masahif).

Wa-athaaran fi al-ardi (and monuments in the earth), but that did not benefit them when Allah seized them for their sins; and they had no protector from Allah, meaning from the punishment of Allah, one who could benefit them or repel it from them. Dhalika bi-annahum kanat ta'tihim rusuluhum bil-bayyinati fa-kafaru fa-akhadhahumu Allah (That was because their messengers came to them with clear proofs, but they disbelieved, so Allah seized them). Innahu qawiyyun shadidu al-'iqab (Indeed He is Powerful, Severe in punishment).

Wa-laqad arsalna Musa bi-ayatina wa-sultanin mubin (And We certainly sent Moses with Our signs and a clear authority) ila Fir'awna wa-Hamana wa-Qarun (to Pharaoh, Haman, and Qarun), fa-qalu sahirun kadhdhab (and they said: a sorcerer, a liar). Fa-lamma ja'ahum bil-haqqi min 'indina (So when he came to them with the truth from Us), qalu (they said), meaning Pharaoh and his people: Uqtulu abna'a alladhina amanu ma'ahu (Kill the sons of those who believed with him).

Qatada said: "This is a killing other than the first killing, because Pharaoh had stopped killing the young boys; then when Moses was sent to him, he resumed killing them."

Wastahyu nisa'ahum (and spare their women), so that by killing the sons and sparing the women they might prevent them from following and supporting Moses. Wa-ma kaydu al-kafirina (And the plotting of the disbelievers is) only in error: the scheming and deception of Pharaoh and his people.

Pharaoh said to his chiefs: Dharuni aqtul Musa (Leave me to kill Moses), wal-yad'u rabbahu (and let him call upon his Lord), whom he claims sent him to us, that He may protect him from us. Inni akhafu an yubaddila (Indeed I fear that he will change) dinakum (your religion) which you are upon, bi-sihr (with magic), aw an...

The reading of Abu 'Amr, the people of Medina, Syria, and Mecca is "wa-an" without alif, and likewise it is in the codices of the people of the two sanctuaries and Syria.

The Kufans and some of the Basrans read "aw an" with alif, and likewise it is in the codices of the people of Iraq.

Abu 'Ubayd said: "It is read with it because of the addition in it, and because 'aw' may sometimes carry the meaning of 'wa', but 'wa' never carries the meaning of 'aw'."

Yuzhira fi al-ardi al-fasad (that he may cause corruption to appear in the land).

The people of Medina and Basra read "yuzhira" with a damma on the yā' and a kasra on the hā', and "al-fasad" with a fatha on the dāl, transitively. Hafs also narrated it from 'Asim in the same way, and this is the choice of Abu 'Ubayd, who said: "He said to his people: yubaddila dinakum, so likewise yuzhira, that the two verbs may be in one pattern."

The others read it with a fatha on the yā' and the hā', and a damma on the dāl, intransitively, and this is the choice of Abu Hatim. Al-fasad is the deterioration of an affair, and Pharaoh meant by it the changing of religion and the worship of other than Him.

Wa-qala Musa, when Pharaoh threatened him with death: Inni 'udtu bi-rabbi wa-rabbikum min kulli mutakabbirin la yu'minu bi-yawm al-hisab (Indeed I have sought refuge in my Lord and your Lord from every arrogant one who does not believe in the Day of Reckoning).

Wa-qala rajulun mu'minun min ali Fir'awna yaktumu imanahu (And a believing man from the family of Pharaoh, who concealed his faith, said). The scholars differed concerning this believer.

Some said: he was from the family of Pharaoh, but he believed in Moses, and he concealed his faith from Pharaoh and his people out of fear for himself.

al-Suddi and Muqatil said: he was the cousin of Pharaoh, and he is the one Allah referred to when He said: Wa-ja'a rajulun min aqsa al-madinati yas'a (And a man came running from the farthest part of the city) [al-Qasas: 20].

Others said: he was an Israelite, and the meaning of the verse is: "And a believing man said, concealing his faith, from the family of Pharaoh."

They also differed about his name.

Ibn 'Abbas and most scholars said: his name was Hizbil.

Wahb ibn Munabbih said: his name was Hizqil.

Ibn Ishaq said: Khabarl.

That is, it drew near. A similar verse is His saying: Azifat al-azifa (The Approaching Hour has drawn near), meaning the Resurrection has drawn near.

Wa-ma tukhfi al-sudur (and what the breasts conceal). Inna Allaha huwa al-sami' al-basir (Indeed, Allah is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing).

Awa lam yasiru fi al-ardi fa-yanzuru kayfa kana 'aqibatu al-ladhina kanu min qablihim, kanu hum ashadda minhum quwwatan (Have they not traveled through the earth and seen how was the end of those before them, who were greater than them in strength).

The common readers read it with the hā' (hum).

Ibn 'Amir read "minkum" with the kāf (you), and likewise it is in their codices (masahif).

Wa-athaaran fi al-ardi (and monuments in the earth), but that did not benefit them when Allah seized them for their sins; and they had no protector from Allah, meaning from the punishment of Allah, one who could benefit them or repel it from them. Ibn Ishaq said: Khabarl.

Then Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) stood up, embraced him from behind, and said: Atqtulna rajulan an yaqula rabbiya Allah wa-qad ja'akum bil-bayyinati min rabbikum (Will you kill a man because he says, 'My Lord is Allah,' when he has come to you with clear proofs from your Lord?), raising his voice with it, and his eyes were pouring tears, until they released him."

He is the One who shows you His signs and sends down for you provision from the sky, by the pouring down of rain; yet none remembers except one who turns back (in repentance). So call upon Allah, sincerely devoting to Him the religion (al-din): worship and obedience, even though the disbelievers dislike it. Rafi' al-Darajat (Exalted in Degrees): He is exalted in degrees, meaning He raises the levels of reward for the prophets and believers in Paradise.

Ibn 'Abbas said: "Rafi' al-samawat (the One who raises the heavens), and He is above everything, and nothing is above Him."

Dhu al-'Arsh (Lord of the Throne): its Creator and its Owner. Yulqi al-ruh (He casts down the Spirit): He sends down the revelation, and He called it "spirit" because by it hearts are given life, just as bodies are given life by spirits. Min amrihi (by His command): from His command, and it was said: by His order. 'Ala man yasha'u min 'ibadihi (upon whomever He wills of His servants), liyundhira yawm al-talaq (that he may warn of the Day of Meeting).

The reading of the common people (al-'amma) is with the yā' (ya), meaning that Allah, the Exalted, warns.

Al-Hasan read it with the tā' (ta), meaning: "that you (tundhir), O Muhammad, may warn of the Day of Meeting."

Abu al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl al-Faqih informed us: Abu al-'Abbas al-Asamm narrated to us: Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd Allah narrated to us: Abu Usama narrated to us: al-Mubarak ibn Fudala narrated to us, from 'Ali ibn Zayd, from Yusuf ibn Mihran, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying, the Exalted: liyundhira yawm al-talaq. He said: "It is the day when the people of the heavens and the people of the earth meet."

Qatada and Muqatil said: "The creation and the Creator meet on it."

Ibn Zayd: "The servants meet one another."

Maymun ibn Mihran: "The oppressor and the oppressed meet, and the disputants." It was also said: "The worshippers and those worshipped meet."

It was said: "A person meets his deeds on it."

Yawm hum barizun (the Day they will come forth): emerging from their graves, visible, with nothing concealing them. La yakhfa 'ala Allahi minhum (nothing about them is hidden from Allah) of their deeds and their states, shay' (anything). The place of "hum" is nominative as a subject (mubtada'), and "barizun" is its predicate. Limani al-mulk al-yawm (Whose is the dominion today?): this occurs at the annihilation of creation, and we have mentioned the reports concerning it.

Al-Hasan said: "He is the one who asks and the one who answers, for He says this when no one answers Him, so He answers Himself: Lillahi al-Wahid al-Qahhar (To Allah, the One, the Subduer), who subdued creation by death."

Shu'ayb informed us: Makki narrated to us: Abu al-Azhar narrated to us: Rawh narrated to us: Hammad narrated to us, from 'Asim ibn Bahdala, from Abu Wa'il, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: "Allah will gather the creation on the Day of Resurrection in one plain, a white land like a silver ingot, in which He has never been disobeyed. The first thing He will say is that a caller will call out: Whose is the dominion today? To Allah, the One, the Subduer."

Al-yawm tujza kullu nafsin bima kasabat, la zulma al-yawm, inna Allaha sari'u al-hisab (Today every soul will be recompensed for what it earned; there is no injustice today; indeed Allah is swift in reckoning). The first thing they will be disputing about is blood.

Wa-andhirhum yawm al-azifa (And warn them of the Day of the Approaching): meaning the Day of Resurrection. It was so named because it is near, since everything that is to come is near.

al-Nabigha said:

"The departure drew near, yet our riding-camels have not yet moved from our saddles, and it is as if..."

That is, it drew near. A similar verse is His saying: Azifat al-azifa (The Approaching Hour has drawn near), meaning the Resurrection has drawn near.

Idh al-qulubu ladaa al-hanajir (When the hearts reach the throats): from fear, the hearts have been dislodged and have risen from their chests, becoming lodged in their throats; so they neither return to their places nor leave their mouths to die, and they are not at ease. Its parallel is His saying: wa-af'idatuhum hawa' (and their hearts are a void). Kazimin (choking, suppressed): distressed, filled with fear and grief. Al-kazim is one who holds back something as it is within it, and from it comes kazama qirbatahu, when he tied its mouth. They have clamped their mouths shut over what is in their hearts of intense fear. Al-kazm is the churning of rage, fear, and grief within the heart when it becomes constricted by them.

The Arabs say of a narrow well and of a full water-vessel: "ma'un kazama and kazima." And from the hadith: "How will you be when Mecca is opened and its ... are filled?"

The poet said:

"They come forth from a narrow well... they carry 'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib."

Kazimin is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (hal) and as a qat' (a separated description).

Ma li al-zalimina min hamimin (The wrongdoers will have no intimate friend), qarib wa-sadiq (close relative and friend), and from it the relatives and close intimates are called hamma. Wa-la shafi'in yuta' (nor any intercessor who is obeyed), so that he may intercede for them.

Ya'lamu khA'inata al-a'yun (He knows the treachery of the eyes).

The author (al-Mu'arrikh) said: "There is inversion (taqdim and ta'khir) in it, meaning al-a'yun al-khA'inah (the treacherous eyes)." Ibn 'Abbas said: "It is the man who sits with a people, and a woman passes by, and he steals a glance at her."

Mujahid said: "It is the eyes' looking at what Allah has forbidden."

Qatada said: "It is the blinking of the eye and its closing regarding what Allah does not love or approve."

Wa-ma tukhfi al-sudur (and what the breasts conceal). Wallahu yaqdi bil-haqq (And Allah judges with truth), wa-alladhina yad'una min dunihi (and those they call upon besides Him), meaning the idols, la yaqdina bi-shay' (they judge nothing), because they know nothing and have no power over anything.

The people of Medina and Ayyub read "tad'una" with the tā' (you), and similarly Hisham narrated from the people of Syria; the rest read it with the yā' (they).

Inna Allaha huwa al-sami' al-basir (Indeed, Allah is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing).

Awa lam yasiru fi al-ardi fa-yanzuru kayfa kana 'aqibatu al-ladhina kanu min qablihim, kanu hum ashadda minhum quwwatan (Have they not traveled through the earth and seen how was the end of those before them, who were greater than them in strength).

The common readers read it with the hā' (hum).

Ibn 'Amir read "minkum" with the kāf (you), and likewise it is in their codices (masahif).

Wa-athaaran fi al-ardi (and monuments in the earth), but that did not benefit them when Allah seized them for their sins; and they had no protector from Allah, meaning from the punishment of Allah, one who could benefit them or repel it from them. Dhalika bi-annahum kanat ta'tihim rusuluhum bil-bayyinati fa-kafaru fa-akhadhahumu Allah (That was because their messengers came to them with clear proofs, but they disbelieved, so Allah seized them). Innahu qawiyyun shadidu al-'iqab (Indeed He is Powerful, Severe in punishment).

Wa-laqad arsalna Musa bi-ayatina wa-sultanin mubin (And We certainly sent Moses with Our signs and a clear authority) ila Fir'awna wa-Hamana wa-Qarun (to Pharaoh, Haman, and Qarun), fa-qalu sahirun kadhdhab (and they said: a sorcerer, a liar). Fa-lamma ja'ahum bil-haqqi min 'indina (So when he came to them with the truth from Us), qalu (they said), meaning Pharaoh and his people: Uqtulu abna'a alladhina amanu ma'ahu (Kill the sons of those who believed with him).

Qatada said: "This is a killing other than the first killing, because Pharaoh had stopped killing the young boys; then when Moses was sent to him, he resumed killing them."

Wastahyu nisa'ahum (and spare their women), so that by killing the sons and sparing the women they might prevent them from following and supporting Moses. Wa-ma kaydu al-kafirina (And the plotting of the disbelievers is) only in error: the scheming and deception of Pharaoh and his people.

Pharaoh said to his chiefs: Dharuni aqtul Musa (Leave me to kill Moses), wal-yad'u rabbahu (and let him call upon his Lord), whom he claims sent him to us, that He may protect him from us. Inni akhafu an yubaddila (Indeed I fear that he will change) dinakum (your religion) which you are upon, bi-sihr (with magic), aw an...

The reading of Abu 'Amr, the people of Medina, Syria, and Mecca is "wa-an" without alif, and likewise it is in the codices of the people of the two sanctuaries and Syria.

The Kufans and some of the Basrans read "aw an" with alif, and likewise it is in the codices of the people of Iraq.

Abu 'Ubayd said: "It is read with it because of the addition in it, and because 'aw' may sometimes carry the meaning of 'wa', but 'wa' never carries the meaning of 'aw'."

Yuzhira fi al-ardi al-fasad (that he may cause corruption to appear in the land).

Some said: he was from the family of Pharaoh, but he believed in Moses, and he concealed his faith from Pharaoh and his people out of fear for himself.

Others said: he was an Israelite, and the meaning of the verse is: "And a believing man said, concealing his faith, from the family of Pharaoh."

They also differed about his name.

Ibn 'Abbas and most scholars said: his name was Hizbil.

Wahb ibn Munabbih said: his name was Hizqil.

Ibn Ishaq said: Khabarl.

Al-Suddi said: "A killer."

It was said: "A person meets his deeds on it."

Yawm hum barizun (the Day they will come forth): emerging from their graves, visible, with nothing concealing them. La yakhfa 'ala Allahi minhum (nothing about them is hidden from Allah) of their deeds and their states, shay' (anything). The place of "hum" is nominative as a subject (mubtada'), and "barizun" is its predicate. Limani al-mulk al-yawm (Whose is the dominion today?): this occurs at the annihilation of creation, and we have mentioned the reports concerning it.

Al-Hasan said: "He is the one who asks and the one who answers, for He says this when no one answers Him, so He answers Himself: Lillahi al-Wahid al-Qahhar (To Allah, the One, the Subduer), who subdued creation by death."

Shu'ayb informed us: Makki narrated to us: Abu al-Azhar narrated to us: Rawh narrated to us: Hammad narrated to us, from 'Asim ibn Bahdala, from Abu Wa'il, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: "Allah will gather the creation on the Day of Resurrection in one plain, a white land like a silver ingot, in which He has never been disobeyed. The first thing He will say is that a caller will call out: Whose is the dominion today? To Allah, the One, the Subduer."

Al-yawm tujza kullu nafsin bima kasabat, la zulma al-yawm, inna Allaha sari'u al-hisab (Today every soul will be recompensed for what it earned; there is no injustice today; indeed Allah is swift in reckoning). The first thing they will be disputing about is blood.

Wa-andhirhum yawm al-azifa (And warn them of the Day of the Approaching): meaning the Day of Resurrection. It was so named because it is near, since everything that is to come is near.

al-Nabigha said:

"The departure drew near, yet our riding-camels have not yet moved from our saddles, and it is as if..."

That is, it drew near. A similar verse is His saying: Azifat al-azifa (The Approaching Hour has drawn near), meaning the Resurrection has drawn near.

Idh al-qulubu ladaa al-hanajir (When the hearts reach the throats): from fear, the hearts have been dislodged and have risen from their chests, becoming lodged in their throats; so they neither return to their places nor leave their mouths to die, and they are not at ease. Its parallel is His saying: wa-af'idatuhum hawa' (and their hearts are a void). Kazimin (choking, suppressed): distressed, filled with fear and grief. Al-kazim is one who holds back something as it is within it, and from it comes kazama qirbatahu, when he tied its mouth. They have clamped their mouths shut over what is in their hearts of intense fear. Al-kazm is the churning of rage, fear, and grief within the heart when it becomes constricted by them.

The Arabs say of a narrow well and of a full water-vessel: "ma'un kazama and kazima." And from the hadith: "How will you be when Mecca is opened and its ... are filled?"

The poet said:

"They come forth from a narrow well... they carry 'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib."

Kazimin is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (hal) and as a qat' (a separated description).

Ma li al-zalimina min hamimin (The wrongdoers will have no intimate friend), qarib wa-sadiq (close relative and friend), and from it the relatives and close intimates are called hamma. Wa-la shafi'in yuta' (nor any intercessor who is obeyed), so that he may intercede for them.

Ya'lamu khA'inata al-a'yun (He knows the treachery of the eyes).

The author (al-Mu'arrikh) said: "There is inversion (taqdim and ta'khir) in it, meaning al-a'yun al-khA'inah (the treacherous eyes)." Ibn 'Abbas said: "It is the man who sits with a people, and a woman passes by, and he steals a glance at her."

Mujahid said: "It is the eyes' looking at what Allah has forbidden."

Qatada said: "It is the blinking of the eye and its closing regarding what Allah does not love or approve."

Wa-ma tukhfi al-sudur (and what the breasts conceal). Wallahu yaqdi bil-haqq (And Allah judges with truth), wa-alladhina yad'una min dunihi (and those they call upon besides Him), meaning the idols, la yaqdina bi-shay' (they judge nothing), because they know nothing and have no power over anything.

The people of Medina and Ayyub read "tad'una" with the tā' (you), and similarly Hisham narrated from the people of Syria; the rest read it with the yā' (they).

Inna Allaha huwa al-sami' al-basir (Indeed, Allah is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing).

Awa lam yasiru fi al-ardi fa-yanzuru kayfa kana 'aqibatu al-ladhina kanu min qablihim, kanu hum ashadda minhum quwwatan (Have they not traveled through the earth and seen how was the end of those before them, who were greater than them in strength).

The common readers read it with the hā' (hum).

Ibn 'Amir read "minkum" with the kāf (you), and likewise it is in their codices (masahif).

Wa-athaaran fi al-ardi (and monuments in the earth), but that did not benefit them when Allah seized them for their sins; and they had no protector from Allah, meaning from the punishment of Allah, one who could benefit them or repel it from them. Dhalika bi-annahum kanat ta'tihim rusuluhum bil-bayyinati fa-kafaru fa-akhadhahumu Allah (That was because their messengers came to them with clear proofs, but they disbelieved, so Allah seized them). Innahu qawiyyun shadidu al-'iqab (Indeed He is Powerful, Severe in punishment).

Wa-laqad arsalna Musa bi-ayatina wa-sultanin mubin (And We certainly sent Moses with Our signs and a clear authority) ila Fir'awna wa-Hamana wa-Qarun (to Pharaoh, Haman, and Qarun), fa-qalu sahirun kadhdhab (and they said: a sorcerer, a liar). Fa-lamma ja'ahum bil-haqqi min 'indina (So when he came to them with the truth from Us), qalu (they said), meaning Pharaoh and his people: Uqtulu abna'a alladhina amanu ma'ahu (Kill the sons of those who believed with him).

Qatada said: "This is a killing other than the first killing, because Pharaoh had stopped killing the young boys; then when Moses was sent to him, he resumed killing them."

Wastahyu nisa'ahum (and spare their women), so that by killing the sons and sparing the women they might prevent them from following and supporting Moses. Wa-ma kaydu al-kafirina (And the plotting of the disbelievers is) only in error: the scheming and deception of Pharaoh and his people.

Pharaoh said to his chiefs: Dharuni aqtul Musa (Leave me to kill Moses), wal-yad'u rabbahu (and let him call upon his Lord), whom he claims sent him to us, that He may protect him from us. Inni akhafu an yubaddila (Indeed I fear that he will change) dinakum (your religion) which you are upon, bi-sihr (with magic), aw an...

The reading of Abu 'Amr, the people of Medina, Syria, and Mecca is "wa-an" without alif, and likewise it is in the codices of the people of the two sanctuaries and Syria.

The Kufans and some of the Basrans read "aw an" with alif, and likewise it is in the codices of the people of Iraq.

Abu 'Ubayd said: "It is read with it because of the addition in it, and because 'aw' may sometimes carry the meaning of 'wa', but 'wa' never carries the meaning of 'aw'."

Yuzhira fi al-ardi al-fasad (that he may cause corruption to appear in the land).

The people of Medina and Basra read "yuzhira" with a damma on the yā' and a kasra on the hā', and "al-fasad" with a fatha on the dāl, transitively. Hafs also narrated it from 'Asim in the same way, and this is the choice of Abu 'Ubayd, who said: "He said to his people: yubaddila dinakum, so likewise yuzhira, that the two verbs may be in one pattern."

The others read it with a fatha on the yā' and the hā', and a damma on the dāl, intransitively, and this is the choice of Abu Hatim. Al-fasad is the deterioration of an affair, and Pharaoh meant by it the changing of religion and the worship of other than Him.

Wa-qala Musa, when Pharaoh threatened him with death: Inni 'udtu bi-rabbi wa-rabbikum min kulli mutakabbirin la yu'minu bi-yawm al-hisab (Indeed I have sought refuge in my Lord and your Lord from every arrogant one who does not believe in the Day of Reckoning).

Wa-qala rajulun mu'minun min ali Fir'awna yaktumu imanahu (And a believing man from the family of Pharaoh, who concealed his faith, said). The scholars differed concerning this believer.

Some said: he was from the family of Pharaoh, but he believed in Moses, and he concealed his faith from Pharaoh and his people out of fear for himself.

al-Suddi and Muqatil said: he was the cousin of Pharaoh, and he is the one Allah referred to when He said: Wa-ja'a rajulun min aqsa al-madinati yas'a (And a man came running from the farthest part of the city) [al-Qasas: 20].

Others said: he was an Israelite, and the meaning of the verse is: "And a believing man said, concealing his faith, from the family of Pharaoh."

They also differed about his name.

Ibn 'Abbas and most scholars said: his name was Hizbil.

Wahb ibn Munabbih said: his name was Hizqil.

Ibn Ishaq said: Khabarl.

Abdullah ibn Hamid informed us: Muhammad ibn Khalid informed us: Dawud ibn Sulayman informed us: 'Abd al-Wahid informed us: Ahmad ibn Yunus narrated to us: Khadij ibn Mu'awiya narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, who said: "The name of the man from the family of Pharaoh who believed was (Habib)."

Atqtulna rajulan an (Will you kill a man because) yaqula rabbiya Allah (he says: "My Lord is Allah"), wa-qad ja'akum bil-bayyinati min rabbikum (when he has come to you with clear proofs from your Lord). Wa-in yaku kadhiban fa-'alayhi kadhibuhu (If he is a liar, his lie is upon him), wa-in yaku sadiqan yusibkum ba'du alladhi ya'iduakum (and if he is truthful, some of what he promises you will befall you), from the punishment.

Some scholars of meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) said: "He meant: all of what he promises you will befall you."

The Arabs mention the part and mean the whole, as in the saying of Labid:

"Your dwellings have become... if I do not inhabit them, or the souls' doves are bound..."

That is, all souls.

Inna Allaha la yahdi man huwa musrif (Indeed Allah does not guide one who is a transgressor): a polytheist.

Al-Suddi said: "A killer."

Kadhdhab (a liar) against Allah.

Al-Imam Abu Mansur Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Jamshadhi informed us: Abu al-'Abbas al-Asamm narrated to us: al-'Abbas ibn Muhammad al-Thawri narrated to us: Khalid ibn Makhlad al-Qatawani narrated to us: Sulayman ibn Bilal narrated to us: Hisham ibn 'Urwa narrated to me, from his father, from 'Amr ibn al-'As, who said: "Nothing was more severe upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) than that when he circumambulated the House, they met him when he finished and seized the edges of his garment, and said: 'Are you the one who forbids us from what our fathers used to worship?'

He said: 'I am that one.'

Then Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) stood up, embraced him from behind, and said: Atqtulna rajulan an yaqula rabbiya Allah wa-qad ja'akum bil-bayyinati min rabbikum (Will you kill a man because he says, 'My Lord is Allah,' when he has come to you with clear proofs from your Lord?), raising his voice with it, and his eyes were pouring tears, until they released him."

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 40, verses 29–37:

"O my people, the kingdom is yours today, dominant (ẓāhirīn), prevailing and exalted over the Children of Israel in the land (fī al-arḍ), the land of Egypt. So who will help us against the might of Allah (ba's Allāh), that is, the punishment of Allah, should it come upon us?" Pharaoh said: "I show you only what I see (mā urīkum) of opinion and counsel, and I guide you only to what I see for myself."

Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: "I do not inform you except of what I know of its like," (based on) "by what Allah has shown you" (Sūrat al-Nisā' 4:105).

"And I guide you only to the path of right conduct (sabīl al-rashād)." And the one who believed said: "O my people, I fear for you a day like the day of the confederates (al-aḥzāb), like the custom (dA'b) of the people of Noah, ʿĀd, Thamūd, and those after them, like what befell them of punishment. And Allah does not desire injustice for His servants. O my people, I fear for you the day of calling out (yawm al-tanād)."

Those in general recited (qara'ahu al-ʿāmma) it with a light dāl, meaning the day when the caller calls out with misery and felicity: "Indeed, so-and-so the son of so-and-so has been made happy with a happiness after which he will never be miserable, and indeed so-and-so the son of so-and-so has been made miserable with a misery after which he will never be happy." People will call to one another; the companions of the heights (aṣḥāb al-aʿrāf) will call out, and the people of Paradise will call to the people of the Fire, and the people of the Fire to the people of Paradise. Death will be slaughtered and it will call out: "O people of Paradise, eternity without death; O people of the Fire, eternity without death." Each people will be called by their deeds. al-Ḥasan recited (al-tanādī) with a light dāl and with the yā' retained, according to the original form.

Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḍaḥḥāk recited with a heavy dāl, in the sense of the day of mutual repulsion (yawm al-tanafur), which is when they flee across the earth as camels flee when they bolt from their herders.

Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: "When they hear the roar of the Fire, they flee in terror; they do not reach any region of the regions except that they find angels in ranks, so they return to the place where they were. That is His saying: 'the day of tanād'." And His saying, exalted is He: "O assembly of jinn and humankind, if you are able to pass through the regions of the heavens and the earth, then pass through; you will not pass except by authority" (Sūrat al-Raḥmān 55:33), and "and the angels will be upon its sides" (Sūrat al-Ḥāqqa 69:17).

"The day you turn back fleeing (yawma tawallawna mudbirīn)," meaning: turning away from the place of reckoning toward the Fire.

Mujāhid said: "It means fleeing, not able to escape."

"You have no protector from Allah (ʿāṣim), no helper who will shield you from His punishment. And whomever Allah leaves astray, for him there is no guide."

"And Yūsuf, son of Yaʿqūb (peace be upon him), came to you before, with clear proofs (bi'l-bayyināt)," meaning: before Mūsā, with the clear proofs.

Wahb said: "The Pharaoh of Mūsā is the Pharaoh of Yūsuf; he lived until the time of Mūsā." The others said: "He is another."

"You remained in doubt about what he brought you, until, when he died, you said: 'Allah will never send a messenger after him.' Thus Allah leads astray whoever is extravagant (musrif), that is polytheist, and a doubter (murtāb), that is one who is skeptical, those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah without any authority that has come to them. It is greatly hateful (kabura maqtan) to Allah," that is, that dispute is greatly hateful, like His saying: "It is greatly hateful to Allah that you say what you do not do" (Sūrat al-Ṣaff 61:3), and "a word that is great (kalimatan) in Allah's sight and in the sight of those who believe" (Sūrat al-Kahf 18:5). "Thus Allah seals (yaṭbaʿu) upon every heart that is arrogant and tyrannical," meaning Allah seals it with disbelief.

Abū ʿAmr and Ibn ʿĀmir recited "qalbin" with tanwīn.

The others recited it with the genitive construction (bi'l-iḍāfa) [[meaning the idāfa of "qalb" to "mutakabbir", and in the speech there is an elision, its estimate being: "Thus Allah seals upon every heart, upon every arrogant tyrant," with "kull" elided.]].

[This was preferred by Abū Ḥātim and Abū ʿUbayd] [[from the tafsir of al-Qurṭubī: 15/313]]. In the recitation of Ibn Masʿūd: "upon the heart of every arrogant tyrant."

Pharaoh said: "O Hāmān, build me a tower (ṣarḥan), a palace. The ṣarḥ is the visible structure that is not hidden from the observer even if far off; its root is from taṣrīḥ, which is manifestation."

"Perhaps I may reach the means (al-asbāb), the means of the heavens," that is, its paths and its gates, "so that I may look upon (fa-aṭṭali'a)."

The general readers recited it with a raised ʿayn, in coordination with His saying "I may reach" (abluḡu).

Ḥumayd al-Aʿraj recited it with a fatḥa on the ʿayn.

Similarly Ḥafṣ narrated from ʿĀṣim, as a response to "perhaps" (laʿallī) with the fāʾ.

Al-Farrāʾ recited from some Arabs:

"Against the vicissitudes of time or its turns, they make us wealthy (yudlinanā) through the poverty of its deprivations,
so the soul rests from its sighs."

with a fatḥa on the ḥāʾ, as a response to the particle of wishing (ḥarf al-tamannī).

"To the God of Mūsā; and indeed I think him a liar" — meaning Mūsā — "in what he says: that he has a Lord other than me who sent him to us." "And thus the evil of his deeds was made attractive to Pharaoh, and he was barred from the path. And the scheme of Pharaoh was nothing but ruin (tabāb), loss and misguidance."

Its like: "Perish the hands of Abū Lahab" (Sūrat al-Masad 111:1).

Those in general recited (qara'ahu al-ʿāmma) it with a light dāl, meaning the day when the caller calls out with misery and felicity: "Indeed, so-and-so the son of so-and-so has been made happy with a happiness after which he will never be miserable, and indeed so-and-so the son of so-and-so has been made miserable with a misery after which he will never be happy." Mujāhid said: "It means fleeing, not able to escape."

"You have no protector from Allah (ʿāṣim), no helper who will shield you from His punishment. And whomever Allah leaves astray, for him there is no guide."

"And Yūsuf, son of Yaʿqūb (peace be upon him), came to you before, with clear proofs (bi'l-bayyināt)," meaning: before Mūsā, with the clear proofs.

Wahb said: "The Pharaoh of Mūsā is the Pharaoh of Yūsuf; he lived until the time of Mūsā." The others said: "He is another."

"You remained in doubt about what he brought you, until, when he died, you said: 'Allah will never send a messenger after him.' Thus Allah leads astray whoever is extravagant (musrif), that is polytheist, and a doubter (murtāb), that is one who is skeptical, those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah without any authority that has come to them. It is greatly hateful (kabura maqtan) to Allah," that is, that dispute is greatly hateful, like His saying: "It is greatly hateful to Allah that you say what you do not do" (Sūrat al-Ṣaff 61:3), and "a word that is great (kalimatan) in Allah's sight and in the sight of those who believe" (Sūrat al-Kahf 18:5). "Thus Allah seals (yaṭbaʿu) upon every heart that is arrogant and tyrannical," meaning Allah seals it with disbelief.

Abū ʿAmr and Ibn ʿĀmir recited "qalbin" with tanwīn.

The others recited it with the genitive construction (bi'l-iḍāfa) [[meaning the idāfa of "qalb" to "mutakabbir", and in the speech there is an elision, its estimate being: "Thus Allah seals upon every heart, upon every arrogant tyrant," with "kull" elided.]].

Ḥumayd al-Aʿraj recited it with a fatḥa on the ʿayn.

Similarly Ḥafṣ narrated from ʿĀṣim, as a response to "perhaps" (laʿallī) with the fāʾ.

Ibn Abbas and Qatadah said: it means the polytheists.

Mujahid said: they are those who shed blood without right.

Ikrimah said: they are the tyrants, the arrogant.

﴿So you will remember what I say to you when you witness the punishment, when remembrance will not benefit you. And I entrust my affair to God.﴾ This is because they threatened him for opposing their religion. ﴿Indeed God is Seeing of His servants,﴾ knowing their affairs, who among them is in the right and who is in falsehood. ﴿So God protected him from the evils of what they plotted.﴾

Qatadah said: he was saved along with Moses, and he was a Copt.

﴿And there befell the people of Pharaoh the worst of punishment﴾, which came down upon them in this world by drowning, and in the Hereafter by the Fire. This is His saying: ﴿The Fire, to which they are exposed morning and evening.﴾ "The Fire" is in the nominative as a substitute (badal) for "the evil punishment." ﴿They are exposed to it morning and evening﴾; the origin of "exposure" (ʿarḍ) is the showing of a thing.

Qatadah said: they are exposed to it morning and evening; it is said to them: "O people of Pharaoh, this is your abode," as rebuke, vengeance and humiliation for them.

Al-Suddi and Hudhayl ibn Shurahbil said: when they perished, their souls were placed in the bellies of black birds, and they are exposed to the Fire every day twice, departing in the morning and returning, until the Hour arrives.

Aqil ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Jurjani informed me that Abu al-Faraj al-Baghdadi, the judge, informed them from Muhammad ibn Jarir: Abd al-Karim ibn Abi Umayr narrated to us: Hammad ibn Muhammad al-Fazari narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Awza'i, and a man asked him, saying: "May God have mercy on you, we saw birds coming out of the sea, heading toward the west, white, in groups, whose number no one knows except God the Exalted. When evening comes, they return like them, black."

He said: "Did you understand that?"

He said: "Yes."

He said: "Those birds have in their crops the souls of the people of Pharaoh; they are exposed to the Fire morning and evening. Then they return to their nests, their feathers burned and turned black. Then white feathers grow on them from the night, and the black ones fall away. Then they go out in the morning, and they are exposed to the Fire morning and evening, then they return to their nests. That is their state in this world. When the Day of Resurrection comes, God the Exalted will say: ﴿Admit the people of Pharaoh into the most severe punishment.﴾"

He said: They used to say that they were six hundred thousand fighting men. [[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 24/90.]]

Ikrimah and Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: this verse indicates the punishment of the grave, because God distinguished the punishment of the Hereafter, saying: ﴿And on the Day the Hour arises: Admit the people of Pharaoh into the most severe punishment.﴾ [[Surah Ghafir: 46.]] "Admit" (adkhilū).

The people of Medina and Kufa, except Abu Bakr and Ya'qub, read it with a hamzah and a kasrah on the kha, from the causative "idkhal" (admit).

The rest read it with a connecting alif and a dammah on the kha, from "dukhul" (enter). [[The meaning is: "Enter, O people of Pharaoh." See the tafsir of al-Qurtubi: 15/320.]]

The people of Kufa said: it is a plural with no singular, since it is like a verbal noun, and its plural is "atbaʿ."

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 40, verses 58–74**

﴿وَمَا يَسْتَوِي الْأَعْمَىٰ وَالْبَصِيرُ وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ وَلَا الْمُسِيءُ ۚ قَلِيلًا مَا تَتَذَكَّرُونَ﴾ With the "ta" (تتذكرون, "you remember"): the people of Kufa and others. With the "ya" (يتذكرون): others.

Abu 'Ubayd preferred this reading, saying: "Because the beginning and end of the verses are a report about a people."

﴿إِنَّ السَّاعَةَ لَآتِيَةٌ لَا رَيْبَ فِيهَا وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ (the Hour is surely coming, there is no doubt about it, but most people do not believe).

﴿وَقَالَ رَبُّكُمُ ادْعُونِي أَسْتَجِبْ لَكُمْ﴾ (And your Lord said: "Call upon Me, I will respond to you"). That is: make Me One and worship Me alone, apart from others; I will answer you, reward you, recompense you, and forgive you. This is the view of most exegetes, and the context of the verse supports it.

Some of them said: it means remembrance, supplication and asking.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to us: Abu Bakr ibn Abi al-Khasib related to us: Uthman ibn Kharadad related to us: Qatar ibn Bashir related to us: Ja'far ibn Sulayman related to us, from Thabit, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Let each of you ask his Lord for all his needs, even for the strap of his sandal when it breaks."

﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ عَنْ عِبَادَتِي﴾ (Indeed, those who are too proud to worship Me): i.e., My Oneness and My obedience. This is from most exegetes.

Al-Suddi said: "from My supplication."

Aqil ibn Muhammad Abu al-Mu'afa ibn Zakariyya informed us: Muhammad ibn Jarir informed us: Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi related to us: Sufyan related to us, from Mansur and al-A'mash, from Dharr, from Sabi al-Hadrami, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Supplication is worship," then he recited this verse: ﴿And your Lord said: "Call upon Me, I will respond to you." Indeed, those who are too proud to worship Me...﴾ — "from My supplication."

And with his chain, from Ibn Jarir: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim related to me: Hisham ibn al-Qasim related to us, from al-Ashja', who said: It was said to Sufyan: "Pray to God." He said: "Abandoning sins is itself supplication."

﴿سَيَدْخُلُونَ جَهَنَّمَ دَاخِرِينَ﴾ (they will enter Hell humbled). Ibn Kathir, Abu Ja'far and Abu Hatim read it with a *damma* on the *ya* and a *fatha* on the *kha* (يُدْخَلُونَ). It is disputed. Abu 'Amr and 'Asim and others read the opposite. (Sana: صاغرين, "abased.")

﴿اللَّهُ الَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ اللَّيْلَ لِتَسْكُنُوا فِيهِ وَالنَّهَارَ مُبْصِرًا ۚ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَذُو فَضْلٍ عَلَى النَّاسِ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ لَا يَشْكُرُونَ﴾. ﴿ذَٰلِكُمُ اللَّهُ رَبُّكُمْ خَالِقُ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ۖ فَأَنَّىٰ تُؤْفَكُونَ﴾ (How then are you turned away?). ﴿كَذَٰلِكَ كَانُوا يُؤْفَكُونَ﴾ — as you were turned away from the truth despite the evident proofs. ﴿كَذَٰلِكَ يُؤْفَكُ الَّذِينَ كَانُوا بِآيَاتِ اللَّهِ يَجْحَدُونَ﴾ (Likewise are turned away those who used to deny the signs of Allah).

﴿اللَّهُ الَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ الْأَرْضَ قَرَارًا وَالسَّمَاءَ بِنَاءً وَصَوَّرَكُمْ فَأَحْسَنَ صُوَرَكُمْ﴾. The general reading of *ṣuwarakum* ("your forms") is with a *damma* on the *ṣad*. Abu Razin al-'Uqayli read *wa-aḥsana ṣiwarakum* with a *kasra* on the *ṣad*, which is a dialect form (lugha).

The common reading is with a *damma* on the *ṣad*.

﴿وَرَزَقَكُمْ مِنَ الطَّيِّبَاتِ ۚ ذَٰلِكُمُ اللَّهُ رَبُّكُمْ ۖ فَتَبَارَكَ اللَّهُ رَبُّ الْعَالَمِينَ﴾ ﴿هُوَ الْحَيُّ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ فَادْعُوهُ مُخْلِصِينَ لَهُ الدِّينَ ۗ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ﴾ ﴿قُلْ إِنِّي نُهِيتُ أَنْ أَعْبُدَ الَّذِينَ تَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ لَمَّا جَاءَنِيَ الْبَيِّنَاتُ مِنْ رَبِّي وَأُمِرْتُ أَنْ أُسْلِمَ لِرَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ﴾. This was when he was called to disbelief, so he was commanded to say this.

﴿هُوَ الَّذِي خَلَقَكُمْ مِنْ تُرَابٍ ثُمَّ مِنْ نُطْفَةٍ ثُمَّ مِنْ عَلَقَةٍ ثُمَّ يُخْرِجُكُمْ طِفْلًا﴾: i.e., children (atfal). Its parallel is: ﴿أَوِ الطِّفْلِ الَّذِينَ لَمْ يَظْهَرُوا عَلَىٰ عَوْرَاتِ النِّسَاءِ﴾ (Surah al-Nur 24:31). ﴿ثُمَّ لِتَبْلُغُوا أَشُدَّكُمْ ثُمَّ لِتَكُونُوا شُيُوخًا﴾ — and among you is he who dies before reaching old age. ﴿وَلِتَبْلُغُوا أَجَلًا مُسَمًّى﴾ (and that you may reach a specified term): a determined time you cannot exceed or precede. ﴿وَلَعَلَّكُمْ تَعْقِلُونَ﴾ (that perhaps you may reason), so that you understand that there is no god but Him.

﴿هُوَ الَّذِي يُحْيِي وَيُمِيتُ ۖ فَإِذَا قَضَىٰ أَمْرًا فَإِنَّمَا يَقُولُ لَهُ كُن فَيَكُونُ﴾.

﴿أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى الَّذِينَ يُجَادِلُونَ فِي آيَاتِ اللَّهِ ۖ أَنَّىٰ يُصْرَفُونَ﴾.

Ibn Zayd said: They are the polytheists.

Most exegetes said: It was revealed concerning the Qadariyya (those who deny divine predestination).

Aqil ibn Muhammad informed me by licence: al-Mu'afa ibn Zakariyya informed us: Muhammad ibn Jarir informed us: Muhammad ibn Bashshar and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us: Mu'ammal related to us: Sufyan related to us, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, who said: "If this verse was not revealed concerning the Qadariyya, then I do not know concerning whom it was revealed." ﴿أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى الَّذِينَ يُجَادِلُونَ فِي آيَاتِ اللَّهِ أَنَّىٰ يُصْرَفُونَ﴾ up to His words ﴿بَلْ لَمْ نَكُنْ نَدْعُو مِنْ قَبْلُ شَيْئًا﴾ to the end of the verse.

And with his chain, from Ibn Jarir: Yunus related to us: Ibn Wahb informed us: Malik ibn Abi al-Khayr al-Zayyadi informed me, from Abu Qabil, from 'Uqba ibn 'Amir al-Juhani, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Among my community, the People of the Book and the People of al-Lin will perish."

'Uqba said: "O Messenger of Allah, who are the People of the Book?"

He said: "A people who learn the Book of Allah and dispute with those who believe."

He said: "And who are the People of al-Lin?" He said: "A people who follow their desires and neglect the prayers." (al-Mustadrak, al-Mu'jam al-Kabir, Jami' al-Bayan.)

Abu Qabil said: "I do not think the deniers of predestination are anyone other than those who dispute with the believers. As for the People of al-Lin, I think they are none other than the people of the 'amud (the tent-dwelling nomads), who have no congregational leader and do not know the month of Ramadan."

Muhammad ibn Jarir said: "The People of the 'amud are the great tribe (al-hayy al-'azim)."

﴿الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِالْكِتَابِ وَبِمَا أَرْسَلْنَا بِهِ رُسُلَنَا ۖ فَسَوْفَ يَعْلَمُونَ ۝ إِذِ الْأَغْلَالُ فِي أَعْنَاقِهِمْ﴾.

Ibn Fanjawayh al-Dinawari informed us: Ibn Habash al-Muqri' related to us: Ibn Fanjawayh related to us: Salama related to us: Abd al-Razzaq informed us: Ibn al-Taymi related to us, from his father, who said: "If one of the shackles of Hell were placed upon a mountain, it would crush it until it reached the black water."

﴿وَالسَّلَاسِلُ﴾: the general reading is with *raf'* (ـُ), as a conjunction to *al-aghlal* (الْأَغْلَالُ).

Ibn Fanjawayh al-Dinawari informed us: Abu 'Ali ibn Habash al-Muqri' related to us: Abu al-Qasim ibn al-Fadl related to us: Abu Zur'a related to us: Nasr ibn 'Ali related to us: my father related to me, from Harun, from 'Amr ibn Malik, from Abu al-Jawza', from Ibn 'Abbas, that he read: ﴿وَالسَّلَاسِلَ يُسْحَبُونَ فِي الْحَمِيمِ﴾ with *nasb* on the *lam* and a *ya*. He said: "When they are dragged by them, it is more severe for them."

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Hadithi informed us: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Sufi related to us: 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz al-Baghawi related to us: my grandfather related to me: Mansur ibn 'Ammar related to me: Bishr ibn Talha related to us, from Khalid ibn al-Duraik, from Ya'la ibn Munabbih, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Allah Most High will produce for the people of the Fire a black, dark cloud, and it will be said: 'O people of the Fire, what do you desire?' They will ask for cold drink. Then it will rain down upon them shackles that increase their shackles, chains that increase their chains, and burning embers that set the Fire ablaze upon them."

﴿ثُمَّ فِي النَّارِ يُسْجَرُونَ﴾: i.e., the Fire is kindled with them.

Mujahid said: "They become fuel for the Fire."

﴿ثُمَّ قِيلَ لَهُمْ أَيْنَ مَا كُنْتُمْ تُشْرِكُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ﴾: meaning the idols. ﴿قَالُوا ضَلُّوا عَنَّا فَلَا نَرَاهُمْ﴾. ﴿بَلْ لَمْ نَكُنْ نَدْعُو مِنْ قَبْلُ شَيْئًا﴾: they denied it. It was said: they were ignorant.

Some said: there is an ellipsis here, meaning: "We did not used to call upon anything before, with sight, hearing, harm, or benefit."

Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: "It means we did not used to do anything before, i.e., our worship of them was lost, so we did nothing."

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿كَذَٰلِكَ يُضِلُّ اللَّهُ الْكَافِرِينَ﴾ (Thus does Allah lead astray the disbelievers).

This is the view of most exegetes, and the context of the verse supports it.

Some of them said: it means remembrance, supplication and asking.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to us: Abu Bakr ibn Abi al-Khasib related to us: Uthman ibn Kharadad related to us: Qatar ibn Bashir related to us: Ja'far ibn Sulayman related to us, from Thabit, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Let each of you ask his Lord for all his needs, even for the strap of his sandal when it breaks."

Al-Suddi said: "from My supplication."

Aqil ibn Muhammad Abu al-Mu'afa ibn Zakariyya informed us: Muhammad ibn Jarir informed us: Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi related to us: Sufyan related to us, from Mansur and al-A'mash, from Dharr, from Sabi al-Hadrami, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Supplication is worship," then he recited this verse: ﴿And your Lord said: "Call upon Me, I will respond to you." Abu Razin al-'Uqayli read *wa-aḥsana ṣiwarakum* with a *kasra* on the *ṣad*, which is a dialect form (lugha).

The common reading is with a *damma* on the *ṣad*.

﴿هُوَ الَّذِي يُحْيِي وَيُمِيتُ ۖ فَإِذَا قَضَىٰ أَمْرًا فَإِنَّمَا يَقُولُ لَهُ كُن فَيَكُونُ﴾.

﴿أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى الَّذِينَ يُجَادِلُونَ فِي آيَاتِ اللَّهِ ۖ أَنَّىٰ يُصْرَفُونَ﴾.

Ibn Zayd said: They are the polytheists.

Most exegetes said: It was revealed concerning the Qadariyya (those who deny divine predestination).

Aqil ibn Muhammad informed me by licence: al-Mu'afa ibn Zakariyya informed us: Muhammad ibn Jarir informed us: Muhammad ibn Bashshar and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us: Mu'ammal related to us: Sufyan related to us, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, who said: "If this verse was not revealed concerning the Qadariyya, then I do not know concerning whom it was revealed." ﴿أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى الَّذِينَ يُجَادِلُونَ فِي آيَاتِ اللَّهِ أَنَّىٰ يُصْرَفُونَ﴾ up to His words ﴿بَلْ لَمْ نَكُنْ نَدْعُو مِنْ قَبْلُ شَيْئًا﴾ to the end of the verse.

And with his chain, from Ibn Jarir: Yunus related to us: Ibn Wahb informed us: Malik ibn Abi al-Khayr al-Zayyadi informed me, from Abu Qabil, from 'Uqba ibn 'Amir al-Juhani, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Among my community, the People of the Book and the People of al-Lin will perish."

'Uqba said: "O Messenger of Allah, who are the People of the Book?"

He said: "A people who learn the Book of Allah and dispute with those who believe."

He said: "And who are the People of al-Lin?" He said: "A people who follow their desires and neglect the prayers." (al-Mustadrak, al-Mu'jam al-Kabir, Jami' al-Bayan.)

Abu Qabil said: "I do not think the deniers of predestination are anyone other than those who dispute with the believers. Muhammad ibn Jarir said: "The People of the 'amud are the great tribe (al-hayy al-'azim)."

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿كَذَٰلِكَ يُضِلُّ اللَّهُ الْكَافِرِينَ﴾ (Thus does Allah lead astray the disbelievers).

Abu 'Ubayd preferred this reading, saying: "Because the beginning and end of the verses are a report about a people."

﴿وَقَالَ رَبُّكُمُ ادْعُونِي أَسْتَجِبْ لَكُمْ﴾ (And your Lord said: "Call upon Me, I will respond to you"). This is the view of most exegetes, and the context of the verse supports it.

Some of them said: it means remembrance, supplication and asking.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to us: Abu Bakr ibn Abi al-Khasib related to us: Uthman ibn Kharadad related to us: Qatar ibn Bashir related to us: Ja'far ibn Sulayman related to us, from Thabit, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Let each of you ask his Lord for all his needs, even for the strap of his sandal when it breaks."

﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ عَنْ عِبَادَتِي﴾ (Indeed, those who are too proud to worship Me): i.e., My Oneness and My obedience. This is from most exegetes.

Al-Suddi said: "from My supplication."

Aqil ibn Muhammad Abu al-Mu'afa ibn Zakariyya informed us: Muhammad ibn Jarir informed us: Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi related to us: Sufyan related to us, from Mansur and al-A'mash, from Dharr, from Sabi al-Hadrami, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Supplication is worship," then he recited this verse: ﴿And your Lord said: "Call upon Me, I will respond to you." Indeed, those who are too proud to worship Me...﴾ — "from My supplication."

And with his chain, from Ibn Jarir: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim related to me: Hisham ibn al-Qasim related to us, from al-Ashja', who said: It was said to Sufyan: "Pray to God." He said: "Abandoning sins is itself supplication."

﴿اللَّهُ الَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ اللَّيْلَ لِتَسْكُنُوا فِيهِ وَالنَّهَارَ مُبْصِرًا ۚ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَذُو فَضْلٍ عَلَى النَّاسِ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ لَا يَشْكُرُونَ﴾. ﴿ذَٰلِكُمُ اللَّهُ رَبُّكُمْ خَالِقُ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ۖ فَأَنَّىٰ تُؤْفَكُونَ﴾ (How then are you turned away?). ﴿كَذَٰلِكَ كَانُوا يُؤْفَكُونَ﴾ — as you were turned away from the truth despite the evident proofs. ﴿كَذَٰلِكَ يُؤْفَكُ الَّذِينَ كَانُوا بِآيَاتِ اللَّهِ يَجْحَدُونَ﴾ (Likewise are turned away those who used to deny the signs of Allah).

Abu Razin al-'Uqayli read *wa-aḥsana ṣiwarakum* with a *kasra* on the *ṣad*, which is a dialect form (lugha).

The common reading is with a *damma* on the *ṣad*.

This was when he was called to disbelief, so he was commanded to say this.

﴿هُوَ الَّذِي خَلَقَكُمْ مِنْ تُرَابٍ ثُمَّ مِنْ نُطْفَةٍ ثُمَّ مِنْ عَلَقَةٍ ثُمَّ يُخْرِجُكُمْ طِفْلًا﴾: i.e., children (atfal). ﴿هُوَ الَّذِي يُحْيِي وَيُمِيتُ ۖ فَإِذَا قَضَىٰ أَمْرًا فَإِنَّمَا يَقُولُ لَهُ كُن فَيَكُونُ﴾.

﴿أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى الَّذِينَ يُجَادِلُونَ فِي آيَاتِ اللَّهِ ۖ أَنَّىٰ يُصْرَفُونَ﴾.

Ibn Zayd said: They are the polytheists.

Most exegetes said: It was revealed concerning the Qadariyya (those who deny divine predestination).

Aqil ibn Muhammad informed me by licence: al-Mu'afa ibn Zakariyya informed us: Muhammad ibn Jarir informed us: Muhammad ibn Bashshar and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us: Mu'ammal related to us: Sufyan related to us, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, who said: "If this verse was not revealed concerning the Qadariyya, then I do not know concerning whom it was revealed." ﴿أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى الَّذِينَ يُجَادِلُونَ فِي آيَاتِ اللَّهِ أَنَّىٰ يُصْرَفُونَ﴾ up to His words ﴿بَلْ لَمْ نَكُنْ نَدْعُو مِنْ قَبْلُ شَيْئًا﴾ to the end of the verse.

And with his chain, from Ibn Jarir: Yunus related to us: Ibn Wahb informed us: Malik ibn Abi al-Khayr al-Zayyadi informed me, from Abu Qabil, from 'Uqba ibn 'Amir al-Juhani, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Among my community, the People of the Book and the People of al-Lin will perish."

'Uqba said: "O Messenger of Allah, who are the People of the Book?"

He said: "A people who learn the Book of Allah and dispute with those who believe."

He said: "And who are the People of al-Lin?" He said: "A people who follow their desires and neglect the prayers." (al-Mustadrak, al-Mu'jam al-Kabir, Jami' al-Bayan.)

Abu Qabil said: "I do not think the deniers of predestination are anyone other than those who dispute with the believers. As for the People of al-Lin, I think they are none other than the people of the 'amud (the tent-dwelling nomads), who have no congregational leader and do not know the month of Ramadan."

Muhammad ibn Jarir said: "The People of the 'amud are the great tribe (al-hayy al-'azim)."

﴿الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِالْكِتَابِ وَبِمَا أَرْسَلْنَا بِهِ رُسُلَنَا ۖ فَسَوْفَ يَعْلَمُونَ ۝ إِذِ الْأَغْلَالُ فِي أَعْنَاقِهِمْ﴾.

Ibn Fanjawayh al-Dinawari informed us: Ibn Habash al-Muqri' related to us: Ibn Fanjawayh related to us: Salama related to us: Abd al-Razzaq informed us: Ibn al-Taymi related to us, from his father, who said: "If one of the shackles of Hell were placed upon a mountain, it would crush it until it reached the black water."

Ibn Fanjawayh al-Dinawari informed us: Abu 'Ali ibn Habash al-Muqri' related to us: Abu al-Qasim ibn al-Fadl related to us: Abu Zur'a related to us: Nasr ibn 'Ali related to us: my father related to me, from Harun, from 'Amr ibn Malik, from Abu al-Jawza', from Ibn 'Abbas, that he read: ﴿وَالسَّلَاسِلَ يُسْحَبُونَ فِي الْحَمِيمِ﴾ with *nasb* on the *lam* and a *ya*. He said: "When they are dragged by them, it is more severe for them."

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Hadithi informed us: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Sufi related to us: 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz al-Baghawi related to us: my grandfather related to me: Mansur ibn 'Ammar related to me: Bishr ibn Talha related to us, from Khalid ibn al-Duraik, from Ya'la ibn Munabbih, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Allah Most High will produce for the people of the Fire a black, dark cloud, and it will be said: 'O people of the Fire, what do you desire?'
